program: Home safety repairs and extreme heat assistance
priceScope: Conditional annual whole-recipient cost divided by a limited modeled local channel; not a verified marginal gift offer or complete portfolio EV

what: Rebuilding Together Houston repairs homes for low-income homeowners, including older adults, veterans and families.
Its Harris County services address roofs, flooring, electrical hazards, accessibility and unsafe heating or cooling conditions.
It uses contractors, volunteers and community partnerships to help residents remain in safer homes.
strengths: The current Harris County window air-conditioning and heating program identifies a concrete heat-exposure mechanism.
Original returns and Schedule D identify donated professional resources omitted from the tax expense line.
Free repairs can address safety and housing burdens faced by households with limited resources.
reservations: No verified unique current annual repair cohort or controlled local health effect was recovered.
The numerical health utility and actual expenditure savings are unsupported conditional priors.
City-selected construction, grants and volunteer resources complicate incremental donor attribution.

sections.what: Rebuilding Together Houston repairs homes for low-income homeowners, including older adults, veterans and families. Its Harris County services address roofs, flooring, electrical hazards, accessibility and unsafe heating or cooling conditions. It uses contractors, volunteers and community partnerships to help residents remain in safer homes.
sections.monitoring: The original return describes hundreds of families each year but provides no verified unique completed cohort used here. Its 43-year cumulative neighbors figure is not annualized. Current 2025 annual report exists; PDF web extraction failed, so no unverified count is adopted. Request unique occupied homes, repair type and completion, household overlap, indoor temperature or exposure change, alternative city-funded work, actual out-of-pocket expenditure avoided, energy bills and maintenance costs.
sections.qualitative: The current Harris County window air-conditioning and heating program identifies a concrete heat-exposure mechanism. Original returns and Schedule D identify donated professional resources omitted from the tax expense line. Free repairs can address safety and housing burdens faced by households with limited resources. No verified unique current annual repair cohort or controlled local health effect was recovered. The numerical health utility and actual expenditure savings are unsupported conditional priors. City-selected construction, grants and volunteer resources complicate incremental donor attribution. Original EIN 76-0027902 confirms the recipient. Free installation establishes service delivery, not measured avoided injury or morbidity. A claimed 20-year extension of home life is not 20 years of health utility. Construction program government-selected scope and contracts may replace or complement grant-funded work.
sections.cost: The conditional limited-channel reference is $112.95 million per ten combined healthy-year welfare equivalents, including 0.148896 clinical QALYs and 0.220218 resource equivalents. $10,000 corresponds to 0.000885 combined equivalents under proportional annual accounting, not a verified next-gift return. Full recognized annual resources $4,169,236 are divided by a judged 150 annual household opportunities × .4 additional implementation = 60 household proxies. One welfare-equivalent adult per household is modeled; clinical subgroup 15 is within the resource union, avoiding additional population inflation. .01 clinical utility for one finite year is a weak symptom/heat-exposure hypothesis, not a trial-derived injury, mortality or home-life conversion. Independent resource success .5 with $1,000 actual otherwise-paid repair, relocation or care expense avoided is a judgment after alternative public repairs, assistance, taxes and substitution; it is not donated repair retail value, capital asset appreciation or property wealth. Positive overlap .5 minus full $100 one-off disruption, increased energy, maintenance or foregone-work burden gives successes $400 net, other exposed households −$100. The same household components are netted before a single log at $20,000 annual consumption; negative gains and all costs remain full. ResourceYears is fraction of one year's gains, not repeated repair spending. Clinical failure retains household resources and burdens; union harms are retained independently. Provider/contractor opportunity costs are distinct from household disruption. Matched counterparty/provider scenarios are explicit stresses; central unknown-neutral zero does not claim complete world net benefit. Whole recipient annual denominator versus this narrow channel is not complete portfolio or marginal gift EV.
sections.funding: Full recognized resource cost is FY2024 $4,013,888 tax expense + $155,348 donated services = $4,169,236; FY2023 $3,575,146 + $109,150 = $3,684,296; FY2022 $3,809,994 + $343,901 donated services + $31,576 direct event expense = $4,185,471. Schedule D donations are added once because excluded from tax expense. Recognized materials and labor already included are not added again. Rental revenue is not a gain or a cost; no populated netted rental expense field was recovered, pending independent alternate-field check. City construction contracts and grants are counterfactual capacity, not automatic donation credit. Current cost, unrecognized volunteer labor and marginal project capacity require due diligence.

model.costScope: Whole annual recipient recognized resources; limited clinical/resource numerator; marginal additional cost unknown
model.geographicAttribution: Harris County narrow repair/heat cohort is entirely inside Houston MSA; g1 assumption excludes any out-of-boundary outcomes.
model.formula: Union=N*unique*b; clinical=union*completion*q*discounted finite years minus full union harms. Financial=.5*people*discounted one-year log(1+joint net gain/baseline), local share once. Headline=10*C/(clinical+financial).
model.counterfactual: Alternative city-selected construction and grant-funded repair, homeowner self-repair, family assistance, energy subsidy and volunteer capacity; additional annual implementation remains a prior.
model.attribution: Annual incremental recipient response is distinct from cohort deduplication and geographic share; no claim of whole annual portfolio or marginal donation causal effect.
model.uncertainty: Source-grounded cost and service description; numerical clinical and disposable-resource effects are unsupported conditional hypotheses. Complete total EV remains unknown.
model.nativeOutcomes: Occupied homes with additional completed safety/heat improvements; finite symptom improvement and actual net household expenses, not repair retail value.
